items.stem: Why must a unique nonce be used for each AES-GCM encryption under the same key?

options.text: Nonce reuse under one key breaks confidentiality and allows forging authentication tags
options.rationale: Correct: GCM nonce reuse is catastrophic, leaking the authentication key material.
Nonce uniqueness is about security, not speed.

options.text: It is only needed when the key is weak
options.rationale: Reuse is dangerous regardless of key strength.
GCM requires a nonce per message.

items.explanation: Correct: GCM nonce reuse is catastrophic, leaking the authentication key material.

items.stem: Why are bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2 preferred over SHA-256 for password storage?

options.text: They are deliberately slow and tunable, resisting brute-force and GPU attacks
options.rationale: Correct: adjustable work factors slow attackers down.
They are intentionally slower, which is the point.

options.text: They do not require a salt
options.rationale: They still use salts; slowness is the differentiator.
Output length is not the security property here.

items.explanation: Correct: adjustable work factors slow attackers down.

items.stem: Which statements about HMAC are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It provides integrity and authenticity using a shared secret key
options.rationale: Correct: HMAC binds a message to a key holder.

options.text: It is stronger than a bare hash for verifying a message came from a key holder
options.rationale: Correct: a plain hash offers no authenticity.

options.text: It encrypts the message so it cannot be read
options.rationale: False; HMAC does not provide confidentiality.

options.text: It eliminates the need for a secret key
options.rationale: False; the shared secret is essential to HMAC.

items.explanation: Correct: HMAC binds a message to a key holder.; Correct: a plain hash offers no authenticity.
